title: Reader TOC long chapter titles wrap and inflate directory rows
symptom: A long real-novel-style chapter title in the reader directory could wrap across multiple lines and make its TOC row much taller than neighboring rows. A Pixel 8 / Android 14 Compose regression reproduced this at 320dp width: the long chapter title measured about 100dp high while a normal single-line title measured about 52dp.
root_cause: ReaderTocSheet constrained long directory scrolling to the selected chapter but did not constrain chapter title text itself. Unlike other reader chrome titles and progress labels, TOC chapter titles were missing single-line overflow handling, so long titles expanded the row height and reduced usable directory density.
fix: Constrained ReaderTocSheet chapter title text to one line.
Rendered overflowing TOC chapter titles with TextOverflow.Ellipsis.
Added a Compose instrumented regression that compares a long real-novel-style chapter title height against a normal single-line TOC title.
failed_attempts: Only asserting that the current chapter is visible in a long TOC does not catch row-height inflation from long chapter titles.
Relying on parser corpus coverage alone does not prove those long titles remain visually usable in the directory sheet.
impact: Keeps the reader directory visually dense and stable for novels with very long chapter names, reducing crowding and accidental selection errors.
